recognize_zh: GMS 銀染色下骨髓組織中布滿大量黑色、大小一致約 2–4 µm 的小型橢圓酵母菌，部分可見窄基出芽並成群聚集，符合莢膜組織漿菌（Histoplasma capsulatum）感染。
features: Numerous small, uniform oval yeast forms stained black with GMS
Size approximately 2–4 µm with occasional narrow-based budding
Organisms clustered in groups consistent with intracellular location within histiocytes
Diffuse distribution throughout the marrow interstitium
Adipocyte spaces present in the green-counterstained background
describe_en: Grocott methenamine silver stain of the bone marrow biopsy highlights innumerable small, uniform, oval yeast forms measuring approximately 2–4 µm, many in clusters consistent with intracellular location, with occasional narrow-based budding. No hyphae or pseudohyphae are present. The organism burden is high and diffusely distributed in the marrow. Findings are consistent with disseminated histoplasmosis; correlation with urine/serum Histoplasma antigen and culture is recommended.

ddx.vs: Cryptococci are larger and more variable in size (4–10 µm or more) with a mucicarmine/Alcian blue positive capsule, unlike the small uniform Histoplasma yeasts.
C. glabrata yeasts are similar in size but are usually slightly larger, not tightly intracellular in histiocytes, and are distinguished by culture or molecular identification.
Pneumocystis cysts are cup- or crescent-shaped with intracystic dots and do not bud.
Talaromyces divides by fission with a central transverse septum rather than budding, and has a travel history to Southeast Asia.
